sources: Ministry of Economic Affairs and Employment
EU Programmes (Horizon Europe, Digital Europe, Innovation Fund, LIFE, CEF)

programs.name: Development Grant (Kehittämisavustus)
programs.description: Support for business development projects to develop products, services, processes, or business models.

eligibility.company_type: SME (Small and Medium Enterprises)
eligibility.annual_turnover: Max EUR 50 million OR balance sheet max EUR 43 million
requirements: Business development project
Aim to improve competitiveness
Cannot be mandatory regulatory requirement
Project not yet started

funding_details.percentage: Up to 50% of development costs (up to 60% for lump-sum projects; investments typically 10-40% depending on region and company size)
funding_details.max_amount: Subject to state-aid and call-specific limits (grants can range from around EUR 10,000 up to several million euros per project)
funding_details.min_project_cost: Minimum grant typically around EUR 10,000 (project must be larger than this)

programs.deadline: Continuous application
programs.application_process: Apply through ELY Centre online service

programs.name: Start-up Grant (Starttiraha)
programs.description: Basic income for new entrepreneurs starting full-time business.

eligibility.company_type: New entrepreneur
requirements: Starting new business
Full-time entrepreneur (min 4 days/week)
Sufficient skills and competence
Viable business plan
Cannot receive overlapping unemployment benefit for the same period

funding_details.amount: Approximately EUR 740 per month (37.21 €/day in 2025, paid for up to 5 days per week; amount is indexed and may change annually)

programs.deadline: Continuous application
programs.application_process: Apply before starting business through ELY Centre

programs.name: Business Loan Guarantee
programs.description: State-backed guarantee from Finnvera for business loans to reduce collateral requirements.

eligibility.company_type: SME
requirements: Viable business plan
Sufficient own financing
Bank loan arranged

funding_details.max_guarantee: Varies by guarantee product (e.g. SME Guarantee up to around EUR 300,000 in total exposure; larger guarantees case-by-case)
funding_details.fee: Risk-based guarantee fee (and possible service fee) charged to the company

programs.deadline: Continuous application

programs.name: Entrepreneur Loan (Yrittäjälaina)
programs.description: Personal loan for a company’s shareholder or business successor to finance ownership arrangements, such as acquiring shares or investing in the company’s share capital.

eligibility.company_type: Shareholder or successor in a limited liability company (SME)
eligibility.company_age: Start-up or established company; target company must have prerequisites for profitable business
requirements: Borrower holds at least 5% of the share capital and votes after the investment or share transaction financed with the loan
Borrower works in the company or serves as a Board member
Borrower’s personal finances are in good order
Target company has prerequisites for profitable business
Loan is used for ownership arrangements (not for working capital, equity boosting of a company in difficulty, or large corporate incentive programmes)

funding_details.amount: Minimum EUR 20,000; final loan amount decided case-by-case according to financing need and borrower’s repayment ability
funding_details.interest_rate: Six-month Euribor + fixed margin of 3.75% p.a. (plus management fee; pricing may change over time)
funding_details.repayment: Loan period typically 5–6 years, maximum 12 years (grace period possible case-by-case)

programs.deadline: Continuous application

programs.name: Finnvera Working Capital Loan
programs.description: Finnvera Loan used to finance working capital needs as part of an overall financing package for SMEs.

eligibility.company_type: SME (and, on special grounds, larger companies)
eligibility.company_size: Typically fewer than 250 employees; turnover max EUR 50 million or balance-sheet total max EUR 43 million
requirements: Start-up or established company with prerequisites for profitable business
Working capital and/or investment financing need in Finland
Overall financing package planned together with a bank or other financiers

funding_details.amount: Minimum EUR 50,000; upper limit decided case-by-case as part of the overall financing package
funding_details.duration: Generally 3–15 years depending on the nature and size of the project
funding_details.collateral: Security negotiated case-by-case (often bank and/or other collateral required)

programs.deadline: Continuous application

programs.name: Finnvera Investment Loan
programs.description: Finnvera Loan used as long-term financing for domestic investment projects such as construction, machinery and equipment, and energy and environmental investments.

eligibility.company_type: SME (and, on special grounds, companies larger than an SME)
eligibility.company_size: Typically fewer than 250 employees; annual turnover max EUR 50 million or balance sheet total max EUR 43 million
requirements: Start-up or established company with prerequisites for profitable business
Investment project in Finland (e.g. construction, machinery and equipment, energy or environmental projects)
Overall financing package planned together with a bank or other financiers
Company operates in a sector Finnvera can finance (e.g. excludes farming, forestry and property development)

funding_details.amount: Minimum EUR 50,000; final loan amount decided case-by-case according to project size and repayment ability
funding_details.duration: Generally 3–15 years depending on the character and size of the investment
funding_details.finnvera_share: Loan is typically part of a financing package with a bank; Finnvera’s share of the total financing is agreed case-by-case

programs.deadline: Continuous application

programs.name: Finnvera Export Credit Guarantee
programs.description: Protection against commercial and political risks in exports.

eligibility.company_type: Exporting companies and banks of all sizes
requirements: Export activities involving Finnish interest (Finnish exporter or significant Finnish content/value-add)
Credit or payment risk related to a foreign buyer, buyer’s bank or buyer’s country
Credit period can be short, medium or long term depending on guarantee type (often used for credit periods over 2 years in larger transactions)

funding_details.coverage: Typically up to 90–95% for commercial risks and up to 100% for political risks, depending on guarantee type and transaction
funding_details.fee: Risk-based premium and handling fees determined case-by-case

programs.deadline: Continuous application

programs.name: Research and Development Funding for SMEs and Midcaps
programs.description: Funding for R&D projects to develop new products, services, production methods or business models for international markets.

eligibility.company_type: SME or Midcap
eligibility.company_size: SME: max 250 employees, turnover max EUR 50M or balance sheet max EUR 43M. Midcap: group-level turnover max EUR 300M.
requirements: Aiming for significant international growth
Developing innovative products, services, production methods or business models
Solution creates competitive advantage in international markets
Creating new expertise for competitive advantage
Sufficient overall financing for the project
Project not yet started at the time of application

funding_details.percentage: Grant: SME research projects 50% of eligible costs (60% if the project content is entirely industrial research); Midcap research projects 40% (50% if entirely industrial research). Loan for development and piloting typically up to 50% of total project costs and up to 70% in justified cases.
funding_details.typical_amount: Projects often range from hundreds of thousands to several million euros depending on scope.
funding_details.min_project_cost: Project budgets are usually at least around EUR 100,000.

programs.deadline: Continuous application

programs.name: Research and Development Funding for Large Companies
programs.description: Grants and loans for large companies to conduct research, development and piloting projects that create new expertise, solutions and international competitive advantage.

eligibility.company_type: Large company
eligibility.company_size: Large company: bigger than an SME or midcap (SME: <250 employees and turnover ≤ EUR 50M or balance sheet ≤ EUR 43M; midcap: group-level turnover ≤ EUR 300M). Companies above this are considered large.
requirements: Genuine aim for significant international growth
Developing new innovative products or services, production methods or business models that will gain a competitive advantage in international markets
Creating new expertise and networks that provide a significant competitive edge
Sufficient self-financing and overall financial soundness
For grant-funded research projects, at least 40% of project costs must be used to purchase services from SMEs and/or research organisations
For loan-funded development and piloting projects, at least 15% of project costs must be used to purchase services from SMEs or research organisations
Project has not started before the funding decision

funding_details.percentage: Grant for research projects: 40% of eligible project costs (50% if the project content is entirely industrial research). Loan for development and piloting can cover up to 50% of total project costs; up to 30% of the loan may be paid as an advance.
funding_details.typical_amount: Project sizes vary from hundreds of thousands to several million euros; there is no fixed public upper limit and the amount depends on project scope and impact.
funding_details.interest: Loan interest rate is three percentage points lower than the official base rate in force, but at least 1% per year; loans are generally granted without collateral and the loan period is typically 7–10 years with 3–5 instalment-free years.

programs.deadline: Continuous application

programs.name: Research and Development Funding for Creative Industries
programs.description: Earmarked R&D funding for companies whose projects renew the creative industries and support bold international growth.

eligibility.company_type: Companies of any size engaged in economic activity with a strong creative industries link (Business Finland does not fund one-person companies)
requirements: Project based on creative skills or solutions for the creative industries
R&D project aiming at bold renewal and international business growth
Cannot finance core content production (e.g. single game, TV series, film, music album, artwork or clothing collection, or routine work generating normal revenue)
Sufficient capabilities and team to steer international growth
Project not yet started at the time of application

funding_details.type: Grant (and in some cases loan, according to Business Finland’s general R&D funding rules)
funding_details.percentage: For small and medium-sized enterprises, development of products, services and business models can be supported with a 35% R&D grant instead of the normal 50% loan; depending on the level of research and company size, support may be higher or lower, or in loan form.
funding_details.typical_amount: Business Finland has earmarked EUR 9 million per year of its funding authorization specifically for R&D in the creative industries from 2025 onwards; individual project funding typically ranges from tens of thousands up to a few million euros depending on scope.

programs.deadline: Call-based; specific funding calls for creative industries R&D are opened with announced application periods (not a fully continuous scheme).

programs.name: Innovative Public Procurement
programs.description: Funding for public procurement units to carry out innovative procurements that renew public services and operations.

eligibility.company_type: Public procurement units (e.g. municipalities, joint municipal authorities, government agencies and other contracting entities covered by the Public Procurement Act)
requirements: Public procurement unit as applicant aiming at long-term development and renewal of its services and operations

Procurement implemented as an innovative procurement (e.g. purchase of a new solution, pre-commercial procurement or catalyst procurement) with cooperation between the procurer, companies and end users
Project size significant enough to boost the sector and, in practice, a large share of the budget (at least around 80%) consisting of research and development activities

funding_details.percentage: Business Finland typically funds around 50% of the project’s eligible costs.
funding_details.typical_amount: Funding is granted case-by-case; supported projects have ranged from hundreds of thousands to several million euros depending on the scope and size of the procurement.

programs.deadline: Continuous application

programs.name: Tempo Funding
programs.description: Business development funding for developing growth strategy and internationalization readiness.

eligibility.company_type: SME or Midcap
requirements: Growth-oriented company
International growth ambition
Developing growth strategy, market entry, or business model
Sufficient own financing

funding_details.percentage: Business Finland grant up to 75% of eligible project costs (company self-financing at least 25%)
funding_details.max_amount: EUR 60,000 per project (max project budget typically around EUR 80,000)
funding_details.min_project_cost: Total project budget typically at least around EUR 30,000

programs.deadline: Call currently closed to new applications (Tempo funding call closed on 3 October 2025)

programs.name: Innovation Voucher (Innovaatioseteli)
programs.description: De minimis aid for SMEs to purchase external expert services to develop a completely new product or service idea with international growth potential.

eligibility.company_type: SME in corporate form (not sole trader, large enterprise, public or non-profit organisation, foundation, association, or Åland-based company)
requirements: Company is in the prepayment register
Credit rating (Rating Alfa, Suomen Asiakastieto) at least A
Full-time entrepreneur in the company for at least 3 months OR at least one full-time employee employed for at least 3 months before applying
New product or service idea with international growth potential (not just further development of an existing product/service)
Need for external expert services to progress the idea
Company has plans for internationalisation
De minimis aid limits not exceeded and no conflicting ongoing Business Finland funding (with specified exceptions in current criteria)

funding_details.amount: Typically EUR 6,000 (covers 100% of the purchased expert services excluding VAT; company can receive the voucher only once)
funding_details.use_of_funds: Purchase external expert services for innovation activities, such as feasibility and marketability studies, demos and prototypes, testing and experiments, IPR and novelty studies, or using research results.
funding_details.notes: Funding criteria and call status have changed over time; always check Business Finland for the latest information.

programs.deadline: Call-based; application windows opened periodically (check Business Finland website for current status).

programs.name: Young Innovative Companies (YIC)
programs.description: Multi-year funding package for young startups with high growth potential.

eligibility.company_type: Young innovative company
eligibility.company_age: Under 5 years old at first decision, max 8 years at end
eligibility.company_size: Small company: under 50 employees, max EUR 10M turnover/balance sheet
requirements: Innovative business model
International growth potential
Min 10% of total costs in R&D in one of the past three financial years
Not continued another company's business (not formed through merger, demerger or acquisition of existing operations)
No profit distribution during the funding period
Opportunity and willingness to obtain external growth funding (e.g. private capital investments)

funding_details.type: Grant (three phases; for companies selected before 1 January 2024 the third phase may instead be a loan)
funding_details.phase1: EUR 250,000 grant (phase 1; typically covers up to 75% of eligible costs)
funding_details.phase2: EUR 250,000 grant (phase 2; typically covers up to 75% of eligible costs)
funding_details.total: Up to EUR 1,000,000 in grants over three phases for companies selected from 2024 onwards (EUR 250,000 + 250,000 + 500,000; earlier funding decisions may have a loan in the third phase instead of a grant)

programs.deadline: Call currently closed to new applications (Young Innovative Companies funding call closed on 10 October 2025; existing NIY projects continue)

programs.name: Production Incentive for the Audiovisual Industry
programs.description: Up to 25% cash rebate for audiovisual productions with eligible production costs incurred in Finland.

eligibility.company_type: Finnish or foreign production companies and other audiovisual companies selected for the production
requirements: Professional audiovisual production (feature film, documentary film, scripted series-type fiction or animation)
Minimum expenditure in Finland at least EUR 500,000
Minimum total production budget: feature film EUR 2,500,000; documentary film EUR 650,000; serial fiction and animation at least EUR 11,500 per finished minute
If the beneficiary is a foreign company, a Finnish production coordinator with a Finnish business ID is required

funding_details.percentage: Up to 25% of eligible production costs incurred in Finland (pre-production, production and post-production); eligible Finnish costs may be a maximum of 80% of the total production budget
funding_details.typical_amount: At least around EUR 125,000 given the minimum EUR 500,000 spend in Finland; actual rebates can reach several million euros for large productions

programs.deadline: Continuous, rolling first-come-first-served while the annual budget remains available

programs.name: Funding for Leading Companies and Ecosystems
programs.description: Funding via challenge competitions for 'leading companies' (Veturi) and their ecosystems to carry out large, long-term R&D and innovation projects that solve major future challenges and significantly increase R&D investments in Finland.

eligibility.company_type: Large globally operating companies or companies aiming to become global players, together with their ecosystems
requirements: Leading company (locomotive) operates globally or has clear potential and commitment to grow into a global player
Ecosystem approach with multiple partners (SMEs, research organisations and other companies)
Addresses major future societal or technological challenges (mission-oriented)
Significant impact on R&D investments, competence, exports and jobs in Finland
Commitment to a multi-year R&D roadmap and ecosystem development

funding_details.type: Grant (Business Finland R&D funding; ecosystem partners may also receive other standard Business Finland R&D instruments)
funding_details.typical_amount: For each challenge competition round, up to EUR 20 million for a leading company and up to EUR 50 million for its ecosystem in the first competition category, and up to EUR 10 million for a challenger company and EUR 20 million for its ecosystem in the second category (total Business Finland budget around EUR 80 million per round).
funding_details.percentage: For leading company projects that mainly involve industrial research, Business Finland grant can be up to 40% of total eligible project costs; ecosystem partners are funded according to normal Business Finland R&D funding rules.

programs.deadline: Call-based challenge competitions; the 2025 round opened on 1 April 2025 with first-phase proposal deadline on 5 September 2025 and funding decisions planned for Q1/2026. Future rounds are announced separately.

programs.name: Funding for Innovation and Growth Research
programs.description: Funding for research organizations studying the impact of global challenges on Finnish businesses and society.

eligibility.company_type: Research or information dissemination organizations (e.g. universities, universities of applied sciences, research institutes)
requirements: Applicant is a research or information dissemination organization whose primary objective is to carry out independent research and/or disseminate research results
Research focuses on the underlying factors of Finland’s innovation environment and growth, and on the impact of global challenges on Finnish businesses and society
Project is aligned with the annual themes and objectives of the Innovation and Growth Research call
Active collaboration with policy makers and policy developers
Strong international cooperation and a multidisciplinary research team

funding_details.percentage: Business Finland’s funding level is 95% for research organizations; no corporate co-financing is required
funding_details.typical_amount: Project sizes are not fixed in the official terms; funded projects are typically multi-year research projects with substantial budgets (exact ranges vary by call)

programs.deadline: Call-based funding: Innovation and Growth Research is opened as a themed research call with annually changing topics; the call for 2025 has ended and future calls will be announced separately.

programs.name: Deep Tech Accelerator (DTA)
programs.description: Funding for deep tech startups commercializing research results to accelerate market entry and international growth.

eligibility.company_type: Startup (limited liability company registered in Finland)
eligibility.company_age: Less than 5 years old at the funding decision for phase 1 (costs accepted until the company is max. 8 years old)
requirements: Founded to commercialise a business idea based on scientific research and related intellectual property
Research-based intellectual property rights and know-how are central to the company’s value creation, market potential and competitiveness
Deep tech solution is still in the product development phase and involves high technological and market-entry risks
Small company: fewer than 50 employees and annual net sales or balance sheet total no more than EUR 10 million
At least 10% of the company’s total costs have been allocated to research and development in one of the previous three financial years
Company has at least one full financial year completed
Company has not continued another company’s business and has not been established through a merger (with only limited exceptions)
Company is not listed and has not distributed profits (e.g. dividends or returns of unrestricted equity)
Full-time founding team with credible expertise in both technology and business development
Credible financing plan and sufficient total funding (self-financing and external finance) secured for the DTA phase and other company operations
Willingness and prerequisites to raise further investments in the company

funding_details.percentage: Business Finland covers up to 75% of approved project costs in each phase; the first two phases are grants and the third phase is a loan
funding_details.amount: Three phases of up to EUR 400,000 each (total funding package up to EUR 1,200,000 per company, subject to call and funding decision)
funding_details.duration: Each phase is estimated to last 12–18 months; continuation to the next phase depends on meeting agreed goals

programs.deadline: Call-based; DTA funding is granted via specific funding calls (e.g. DTA 2025 call), with application deadlines announced on Business Finland’s website

programs.name: Energy Aid
programs.description: Support for renewable energy, energy efficiency, and energy system projects.

eligibility.company_type: All sizes
requirements: Renewable energy production project, energy efficiency improvement or energy system flexibility project
Project not yet started before the aid decision
Investment costs of the project between EUR 30,000 and EUR 5,000,000

funding_details.percentage: Typically 15–30% of eligible costs; for some new-technology projects the rate can be higher in line with the current decree
funding_details.max_amount: Eligible investment costs up to EUR 5,000,000 per project

programs.deadline: Continuous application within the current aid scheme period

programs.name: Innovation Aid for Shipbuilding
programs.description: Government subsidy for companies in the shipbuilding sector to develop and market advanced, innovative ship or offshore solutions that are new in the sector or significantly better than current leading solutions.

eligibility.company_type: Companies operating in the shipbuilding sector (shipbuilding, ship repair, ship modification, floating and moving offshore structures)
requirements: Company is registered in Finland and has an office in Finland
Project involves the experimental development of an innovative product or method in shipbuilding
Product or process is technically new or significantly better than the current leading solutions in the EU shipbuilding industry
Application is submitted before the ship order is placed (the aid is granted only after the company has received the order)
Company has the potential for continued profitable operations and meets Business Finland’s general funding conditions

funding_details.percentage: Grant may not exceed 25% of the eligible costs defined in the Government Decree on state aid for innovations in shipbuilding
funding_details.typical_amount: For a single project, Business Finland can grant up to EUR 25 million; actual grant size is determined case-by-case based on eligible innovation costs

programs.deadline: Ongoing scheme; applications must be submitted before the ship order is placed (aid granted after the order has been received)

programs.name: European Defense Fund National Co-Funding
programs.description: National co-funding for Finnish participants in European Defense Fund (EDF) defence research and development projects, complementing EU funding and allowing public funding to cover up to 90% of project costs.

eligibility.company_type: Finnish startups, SMEs, large companies and research organizations
requirements: Project has received EDF funding and an EDF Grant Agreement is or will be signed with the European Commission
Applicant is a Finnish startup, SME, large company or research organization participating in the EDF project
Defense R&D project that significantly strengthens Europe’s defence capabilities and technological self-sufficiency
Meets Business Finland’s national R&D funding criteria

funding_details.type: Grant (national complementary co-funding for EDF projects)
funding_details.percentage: Together with EDF funding, public funding (EDF + national co-funding) can cover up to 90% of the project costs; Business Finland’s share is determined case-by-case based on the Commission’s Grant Agreement and project cost structure.
funding_details.typical_amount: Varies according to EDF project size and EU contribution; Business Finland does not publish a fixed minimum or maximum amount for national co-funding.

programs.deadline: Call-specific. For the EDF 2025 call, applicants must submit a national co-funding application via Business Finland’s online service at the latest when the Ministry of Defence forwards the support request to Business Finland; for EDF 2024 projects, applications for complementary funding must be submitted within 90 days from signing the EDF Grant Agreement. Future calls may have updated timelines, so applicants should always follow the current guidance on the Business Finland EDF National Co-Funding page.

programs.name: Preparatory Funding for Horizon, EDF and Innovation Fund Projects
programs.description: Preparatory funding for companies to plan large Horizon Europe, European Defence Fund (EDF) and Innovation Fund projects, including consortium building and application preparation.

eligibility.company_type: Companies of all sizes operating in Finland (SMEs and large companies)
requirements: Preparing a Horizon Europe, EDF or Innovation Fund project application
For Horizon Europe / EDF preparation: EU project total budget at least EUR 3 million
Preparatory project costs may be at most 5% of the participant’s total costs in the planned EU project
For Horizon Europe / EDF: Finnish partner has a significant role in an extensive consortium (partners from at least three EU or associated countries)
Personnel in Finland at least 2 FTE, of which at least one is a full-time employee
Net financial assets in the balance sheet at least equal to the total costs of the preparatory project
For Innovation Fund preparation: project sufficiently mature in terms of technical planning, business model and financial/legal structure
For Innovation Fund preparation: the company’s board has not yet made the final investment decision and the company can cover its required own financing share
Funding is de minimis aid (max EUR 300,000 de minimis aid over three fiscal years, aggregated at group/control level)

funding_details.percentage: For Horizon Europe and EDF preparation: up to 75% of eligible preparation costs; for Innovation Fund preparation: up to 50% of eligible preparation costs (in both cases, preparatory project costs may not exceed 5% of the participant’s total costs in the planned EU project).
funding_details.max_amount: For Horizon Europe and EDF: maximum EUR 60,000 per company; for Innovation Fund: maximum EUR 200,000 per company.
funding_details.notes: No advance payment; costs can be reported once the EU application has been evaluated and meets the minimum threshold scores of the respective EU programme.

programs.deadline: Continuous call in principle; however, the application period is temporarily closed from 10 November 2025 at 23:59 until further notice due to grant authorisation constraints (no new or incomplete applications can be submitted while closed).

programs.name: Investment Aid for Large Clean Transition Investments
programs.description: Grant aid for large industrial investment projects (eligible costs of at least EUR 30 million) that decarbonise production processes, improve energy efficiency or support the transition to a climate-neutral economy in Finland.

eligibility.company_type: Industrial companies of all sizes investing in Finland (excluding the territory of Åland)
requirements: Investment project carried out in Finland (excluding Åland)
Eligible investment costs of at least EUR 30 million
Project significantly advances Finland’s climate and economic policy objectives

Either reduces direct greenhouse gas emissions from industrial installations by at least 40% OR reduces energy consumption for the supported activity by at least 20% compared to the situation prior to the aid
Company is not in difficulty and not subject to EU sanctions
Company is in the prepayment register and has no significant tax debts or enforcement debts without a valid payment plan
No outstanding recovery order from a previous EU state aid decision
Application submitted before the start of works (before binding commitments that make the investment irreversible)

funding_details.percentage: For decarbonisation and energy efficiency investments: up to 50% of eligible costs for investments reducing greenhouse gas emissions (excluding electrification), and up to 30% for investments related to electrification that reduce emissions or for investments that reduce energy consumption. For investments in sectors strategic to the climate-neutral transition, aid is generally up to 15% of eligible costs (up to 20% in assisted areas).
funding_details.typical_amount: Aid is granted case-by-case; in the 2025 call, individual grants have been in the tens of millions of euros, with large projects receiving support exceeding EUR 100 million.
funding_details.max_aid: The grant may not exceed EUR 200,000,000 per company/undertaking. If the same investment also receives a tax credit for large clean transition investments, the combined amount of grant and tax credit may not exceed EUR 200,000,000 (for some strategic-sector investments outside assisted areas, a lower EUR 150,000,000 ceiling applies).

programs.deadline: Grant call closed (the published call has ended and the grant is currently not available for new applications).

programs.name: Tax Credit for Large Clean Transition Investments
programs.description: Investment rebate (tax credit) for large investments (eligible costs of at least EUR 50 million) in Finland that support the transition to a climate-neutral economy, including renewable energy production and storage, decarbonisation and energy efficiency of industrial processes, and the production of equipment, components and critical raw materials that are strategic for the climate-neutral transition.

eligibility.company_type: Companies of all sizes making eligible investments in Finland (excluding credit and other financial institutions, and companies in difficulty)
requirements: Eligible investment costs of at least EUR 50 million in Finland

Investment in one of the following: energy production from renewable sources and energy storage; decarbonisation of industrial production processes and energy efficiency measures; or production of equipment, components or critical raw materials strategic for the transition to a climate-neutral economy
Project work has not started before applying for the investment credit (application must be submitted before the start of works)
Company is not in difficulty and is not a credit or other financial institution
No outstanding recovery order for unlawful state aid and company/group/controlling owners are not on the EU sanctions list

funding_details.percentage: 20% of costs accepted as the basis for the investment credit
funding_details.calculation: Tax credit of 20% of eligible investment costs, granted by Business Finland, deducted from corporate income tax starting from the tax year beginning in 2028 and the following 19 tax years; in each tax year a maximum of 10% of the total credit may be deducted (subject to the investment being completed).
funding_details.typical_amount: Varies by project; for eligible investments of at least EUR 50,000,000 the tax credit can reach tens of millions of euros, with a statutory maximum of EUR 150,000,000 per company or group.

programs.deadline: Application period has ended; the tax credit is no longer available for new applications under the current scheme.

programs.name: Circular Economy Investment Grant
programs.description: Grant for circular economy investments by companies operating in Finland that improve the level of environmental protection beyond EU standards or increase waste recycling with solutions that exceed the current level of technical development.

eligibility.company_type: All sizes (companies registered and operating in mainland Finland)
requirements: Improves environmental protection beyond EU standards OR increases waste recycling beyond the current level of technological development
Investment in circular economy in Finland with significant environmental impact and potential for business and employment growth
Company has financial prerequisites to cover its self-financing share and to operate profitably
Project not yet started at the time of application
Company is in the prepayment register and has no significant unarranged tax or payment defaults
Company is not an undertaking in difficulty as defined in EU state aid rules (with specific COVID-era exceptions)

funding_details.percentage: Maximum aid intensity for additional investment costs: up to 45% for SMEs and up to 35% for large companies (incl. midcap), determined case-by-case in line with EU state aid rules.
funding_details.typical_amount: The maximum grant for a single company and project is EUR 15,000,000; actual grant amounts vary by project size and eligible additional costs.

programs.deadline: Currently no open call for new applications; previous calls were implemented under Finland's Sustainable Growth Programme (RRF).

programs.name: Funding for Business Development in Disruptive Circumstances
programs.description: Temporary grant funding instrument used mainly during the COVID-19 crisis to support companies in developing their business, products and services in disruptive market circumstances. The scheme is no longer open to new applications.

eligibility.company_type: SMEs employing 6–250 people and midcap companies (larger than SME but with group turnover under EUR 300 million)
requirements: Company employs at least 6 people (including entrepreneur(s)) at the time of application
Company had viable business and prerequisites for profitability before the disruptive situation (e.g. COVID-19)
Company is not a firm in difficulty under EU state aid rules
Applicant is not a large company, private trader, public organisation, foundation or company registered in Åland
Funding used for development of business operations and/or new products and services, not for covering losses, fixed costs or pure working capital
Project activities are new to the company and project had not started before the application

funding_details.percentage: Grant covered up to 80% of approved project costs (company self-financing at least 20%)
funding_details.typical_amount: Preliminary study: grant up to EUR 10,000 (project size max EUR 12,500). Development funding: grant up to EUR 100,000 (project size max EUR 125,000).
funding_details.use_of_funds: Costs of preliminary analyses and development measures that improve the company’s chances during and after a disruption caused e.g. by the coronavirus (e.g. new business models, digital services, sales and marketing development).

programs.deadline: Program was temporary and is no longer open; used during specific disruptive periods such as the COVID-19 crisis.

programs.name: Business Subsidies (Yritystuki)
programs.provider: Ministry of Economic Affairs and Employment
programs.description: Umbrella term for various business development subsidies and support schemes (such as enterprise development grants and start-up grants) administered via ELY Centres under the Ministry of Economic Affairs and Employment.

eligibility.company_type: SME
requirements: Development project
Regional development impact
Job creation potential

funding_details.percentage: Varies by program

programs.deadline: Program-specific

programs.name: Rural Development Funding
programs.description: Support for rural entrepreneurship and businesses, including agriculture, forestry, food and other rural sectors, mainly financed via the EU rural development fund and Finland’s CAP Strategic Plan 2023–2027.

eligibility.company_type: Rural businesses, agriculture, forestry
requirements: Operating in a designated rural area
Agriculture, forestry, food, bioeconomy or other rural business sector
Development, investment or start-up project that meets CAP and national criteria

funding_details.type: Grant (may be combined with other financing such as loans or interest-subsidised loans)
funding_details.percentage: Typically 20–50% of eligible costs depending on measure, region and beneficiary
funding_details.administered_by: ELY Centres and Leader groups under the Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry (applications usually via the Hyrrä e-service)

programs.deadline: Program-specific application periods

programs.name: Horizon Europe - Pillar 2: Global Challenges and European Industrial Competitiveness
programs.description: Horizon Europe is the EU's 2021–2027 research and innovation framework programme with a budget of EUR 95.5 billion. Pillar 2 provides the largest share of the programme’s budget and funds collaborative research and innovation projects that address major global challenges and strengthen European industrial competitiveness.

eligibility.company_type: All organisation types and sizes (universities, research organisations, SMEs, large companies, public bodies, NGOs, etc.)
requirements: International consortium in most calls: at least three independent legal entities from three different EU Member States or Horizon Europe Associated Countries (unless the specific topic defines other rules)
Research and innovation project responding to a specific call topic under one of the Pillar 2 clusters
Compliance with all call- and topic-specific eligibility, admissibility and evaluation criteria as set out in the Horizon Europe Work Programme and call documents

funding_details.percentage: Research and Innovation Actions (RIA) and Coordination and Support Actions (CSA): up to 100% of eligible direct costs. Innovation Actions (IA): 70% of eligible direct costs (100% for non-profit organisations).
funding_details.project_size: Varies by topic; many collaborative projects have EU contributions in the rough range of EUR 2–15 million.
funding_details.duration: Typically around 3–5 years, depending on the call and project scope.

focus_areas: Food, Bioeconomy, Natural Resources, Agriculture and Environment
programs.deadline: Multiple calls each work programme period, with annual or biennial call deadlines depending on the cluster and topic.
programs.application_process: Applicants identify a suitable topic and submit proposals electronically via the EU Funding & Tenders Portal.

programs.name: Horizon Europe - Pillar 3: Innovative Europe (EIC)
programs.description: Horizon Europe’s Pillar 3 (Innovative Europe) is implemented mainly through the European Innovation Council (EIC), which supports breakthrough and market-creating innovation via three main instruments: EIC Pathfinder, EIC Transition and EIC Accelerator.

eligibility.company_type: SMEs, start-ups, small mid-caps, researchers and research organisations (depending on the specific EIC instrument)
requirements: High-risk, high-impact innovation with clear European and global market potential
Applicants established in an EU Member State or Horizon Europe Associated Country, or willing to establish there before signing the grant or investment agreement
Ambition and capacity to scale the innovation internationally, meeting the excellence, impact and risk criteria set out in the relevant EIC Work Programme call

funding_details.eic_pathfinder: Grants of up to EUR 3–4 million per project (100% funding) for early-stage, high-risk research on radically new technologies, typically for consortia, with some calls open to smaller consortia or single applicants.
funding_details.eic_transition: Grants of up to EUR 2.5 million (100% funding) to validate and demonstrate technologies in relevant application environments and develop business and market readiness.
funding_details.eic_accelerator: Grant funding of up to EUR 2.5 million (typically 70% of eligible innovation costs) combined with an optional equity investment component usually between EUR 0.5 million and EUR 15 million via the EIC Fund.

programs.deadline: Regular cut-off dates for each instrument as defined in the annual EIC Work Programme; EIC Accelerator uses a continuous submission for short applications with several cut-off dates per year for full proposals.

programs.name: Digital Europe Programme - Digital Skills
programs.description: Funding under the Digital Europe Programme (DEP) to design and deliver advanced digital skills education and training, and to strengthen Europe’s digital skills ecosystem.

eligibility.company_type: Public and private organisations (higher education institutions, VET providers, research organisations, companies, public authorities, NGOs) established in EU Member States or Digital Europe Programme-associated countries
requirements: Applicants must be legal entities established in an EU Member State or a country associated to the Digital Europe Programme

Projects are usually implemented by transnational consortia (typically at least 3–4 independent organisations from different eligible countries, often including higher education institutions and industry/research partners)

Proposals must design and deliver education, training or support actions that address advanced digital skills needs (for example in AI, data, cloud/HPC, cybersecurity, semiconductors or other key digital technologies), or strengthen digital skills ecosystems in line with the Digital Europe work programmes
Detailed eligibility conditions (such as minimum numbers of students/trainees, specific target groups and consortium composition) are defined in each call topic on the EU Funding & Tenders Portal

funding_details.percentage: Most advanced digital skills actions are co-funded at 50% of eligible costs; some coordination and support actions (CSA) can receive up to 100% EU co-financing, and certain SME-focused actions may allow a higher rate (for example 75% for SMEs) depending on the call topic
funding_details.typical_project: EU contributions to individual projects commonly range from about EUR 2–10 million, with project durations of roughly 2–4 years; exact grant amounts and budgets are specified in each call topic

programs.deadline: Annual and multiannual calls published under the Digital Europe work programmes (check the EU Funding & Tenders Portal for current deadlines)

programs.name: Digital Europe Programme - AI
programs.description: Funding under the Digital Europe Programme for deploying and scaling artificial intelligence solutions, including testing and experimentation facilities, AI data and cloud infrastructure, and sectoral AI deployment projects.

eligibility.company_type: Companies, research organisations, public sector bodies and other organisations established in EU Member States or associated countries
requirements: Project focused on deployment, testing or uptake of AI (e.g. AI testing and experimentation facilities, AI data spaces, sectoral AI deployment, AI-on-demand platform)
Compliance with the specific topic conditions in the Digital Europe work programme and call text

For most calls, a consortium of independent organisations from multiple eligible countries (typically at least three entities from three different Member States or associated countries), unless the call explicitly allows single applicants
Sound technical and business implementation plan, including measures for trustworthy, lawful and ethical AI, data protection and cybersecurity
Sufficient operational and financial capacity to carry out the project

funding_details.percentage: For deployment projects (simple grants), EU co-funding is typically around 50% of eligible costs; some coordination/support or capacity-building actions can receive up to 100% funding, depending on the call topic and type of action.
funding_details.typical_project: Project budgets commonly range from around EUR 2 million to over EUR 10 million, with some flagship AI testing or infrastructure actions significantly larger; exact size and funding rate are specified per call topic in the work programme.

programs.deadline: Multiple calls published periodically under the Digital Europe work programme; deadlines and topics are announced on the EU Funding & Tenders Portal.

programs.name: Digital Europe Programme - Cybersecurity
programs.description: Funding under the Digital Europe Programme to strengthen EU-wide cybersecurity capacity, infrastructure and skills, including support for cybersecurity infrastructure, operational cooperation, preparedness, skills and deployment of advanced cybersecurity solutions.

eligibility.company_type: Companies, public-sector bodies, research organisations, universities and other eligible entities established in EU/EEA Member States or associated countries (specific calls may be restricted, e.g. to public bodies or national coordination centres).
requirements: Project addresses priorities and objectives in the current Digital Europe cybersecurity work programme (e.g. infrastructure, operational cooperation, skills, tools or services).
Participation in a transnational consortium is required for most calls (typically several entities from different eligible countries), unless a specific call allows single beneficiaries.
Compliance with Digital Europe Programme rules on security restrictions, third-country participation and procurement where applicable.
Project proposal meets the call-specific criteria for relevance, implementation quality and impact as set out in each topic description.

funding_details.percentage: For deployment-type actions, the EU co-funding rate is typically around 50% of eligible costs; some coordination and support actions may be funded at a higher rate (up to 100%). The exact funding rate is defined in each call topic.
funding_details.typical_project: Indicative EU contribution per project often in the range of EUR 3–15 million, depending on the specific cybersecurity call and topic.

programs.deadline: Annual or multi-annual calls published under the Digital Europe Programme cybersecurity work programme (check the EU Funding & Tenders Portal for current open calls).

programs.name: Innovation Fund - Large Scale Projects
programs.description: Support for first-of-a-kind and highly innovative low- and net-zero-carbon projects at commercial scale, helping to decarbonise industry and energy systems in the EU.

eligibility.company_type: All sizes (single applicants or consortia)
eligibility.min_capex: Generally projects with total capital expenditure (CAPEX) above EUR 7.5 million are considered large-scale (some recent calls define higher CAPEX thresholds per topic).
requirements: Innovative low- or net-zero-carbon technology or process that goes beyond the state of the art
Significant, credible greenhouse gas (GHG) emission reductions compared with a reference scenario
Project implemented in an eligible country (EU Member States plus Norway, Iceland and Liechtenstein or other associated countries as specified in each call)
Project sufficiently mature in terms of planning, business model, and financial/legal structure at the time of application
Compliance with call-specific award criteria (innovation level, GHG avoidance, project maturity, scalability and cost efficiency)

funding_details.percentage: Regular Innovation Fund grants can cover up to 60% of the project’s relevant costs (typically additional capital and, for large-scale projects, part of operating costs compared to a conventional reference scenario).
funding_details.typical_award: Many large-scale projects receive grants in the order of EUR 10–100+ million per project, with no formal maximum grant limit set in the general rules.
sectors: Net-zero mobility and other sectors covered by the EU ETS revision

programs.deadline: Calls for large-scale projects are launched periodically (roughly once per year); timelines and topics are defined in each specific call for proposals.

programs.name: Innovation Fund - Small Scale Projects
programs.description: Support for smaller demonstration projects of innovative low-carbon technologies and processes with total capital expenditure between EUR 2.5 and 7.5 million.

eligibility.company_type: All sizes (single applicant or consortium from eligible EU/EEA countries)
eligibility.capex: Total project capital expenditure between EUR 2.5 million and EUR 7.5 million
requirements: Innovative low-carbon technology or process in a sector covered by the EU Emissions Trading System (ETS) or producing low-carbon substitute products
Project located in an eligible EU/EEA country (as defined in the specific call)
Significant greenhouse gas emission reduction compared to a reference scenario
Project meets call-specific criteria on innovation, maturity, scalability and cost-efficiency

funding_details.percentage: Up to 60% of the project's relevant capital costs (CAPEX)
funding_details.typical_award: Up to about EUR 4.5 million (maximum grant for small-scale Innovation Fund projects)

programs.deadline: Annual or periodic small-scale calls published via the EU Funding & Tenders Portal

programs.name: LIFE Programme - Climate Action
programs.description: EU funding under the LIFE Climate Action sub-programme for projects on climate change mitigation, climate change adaptation, and climate governance and information.

eligibility.company_type: Public and private organisations (public bodies, companies, NGOs, research organisations, etc.) from LIFE-eligible countries
requirements: Project relates to climate change mitigation (e.g. renewable energies, energy efficiency, farming, land use, peatland management), climate change adaptation (e.g. resilience to water scarcity, droughts, forest fires or floods, adaptive technologies for economic sectors, safeguarding natural resources), or climate governance and information (e.g. awareness raising, training and capacity building, law compliance and enforcement, knowledge development, stakeholder participation).
Applicant and partners are established in an EU Member State or another LIFE-eligible country according to the conditions of the annual LIFE call.

Project is a best practice, pilot or demonstration project (for mitigation/adaptation) or an information, awareness and dissemination / governance project (for climate governance and information), not pure research.
Project contributes to the implementation and development of EU climate policy and law and delivers concrete, measurable climate benefits.

funding_details.percentage: Climate change mitigation, climate change adaptation, and climate governance and information projects receive co-funding of up to 55% of eligible project costs. Certain other LIFE project types (e.g. integrated, preparatory or technical assistance projects) can receive up to 60% under separate schemes.
funding_details.typical_project: Traditional LIFE Climate Action projects often have total budgets from roughly EUR 0.5–5 million, with LIFE contributions commonly in the range of about EUR 0.5–2 million depending on scope and partnership.

focus_areas: Resilience to Droughts, Forest Fires and Floods
programs.deadline: Annual calls; specific opening and closing dates are published each year under the LIFE Programme call for proposals.

programs.name: LIFE Programme - Nature & Biodiversity
programs.description: EU funding for projects that protect and restore nature, biodiversity and ecosystems, in particular habitats and species and the Natura 2000 network.

eligibility.company_type: All organisations (public and private legal entities) from countries eligible for the LIFE programme
requirements: Project falls under the objectives and priority topics of the LIFE Nature and Biodiversity sub-programme (e.g. conservation, restoration or management of species, habitats or Natura 2000 sites, implementation of EU nature and biodiversity policy)
Applicant is a legal person established in an EU Member State or another country associated with LIFE, as defined in the annual call documents
Project complies with the specific eligibility and admissibility criteria of the relevant LIFE call for proposals (e.g. Standard Action Projects, Strategic Nature Projects)
Proposal is submitted electronically via the EU Funding & Tenders Portal within the call deadline

funding_details.percentage: For Standard Action Projects, EU co-financing is generally up to 60% of total eligible costs; this may increase up to 75% for projects that focus on concrete conservation actions for priority habitats or species and allocate at least 50% of eligible costs to such actions, subject to current call conditions.
funding_details.typical_project: In recent calls, LIFE Nature and Biodiversity projects have often received EU contributions in the range of about EUR 1–10 million per project, depending on scope and project type.

programs.deadline: Annual calls (specific topics and deadlines are published each year on the EU Funding & Tenders Portal)

programs.name: LIFE Programme - Circular Economy and Quality of Life
programs.description: EU grants for projects that advance the circular economy and zero pollution, including recovery of resources from waste and measures to protect, restore and improve the environment and citizens’ quality of life.

eligibility.company_type: Legal entities established in EU Member States or associated countries (public bodies, private companies, NGOs, universities)
requirements: Project clearly contributes to LIFE Circular Economy and Quality of Life objectives (e.g. circular economy, waste, air, water, soil, chemicals, noise, urban environment, environmental governance)
Complies with the specific topic, technical and financial eligibility criteria in the yearly LIFE call

funding_details.percentage: Up to 60% of eligible costs for most projects under this sub-programme (higher rates for some specific LIFE call types)
funding_details.typical_project: EU contribution typically around EUR 2–10 million; total project budgets usually in the low multi-million range

focus_areas: Zero pollution (air, water, soil, noise, chemicals, industrial emissions)
Sustainable management of natural resources and urban environment
Environmental governance and implementation of EU environmental law
programs.deadline: Annual calls (normally opening in late April/May and closing around September; see current LIFE call fiche)

programs.name: Connecting Europe Facility (CEF) for Transport
programs.description: EU grant scheme that co-finances TEN-T transport infrastructure projects, focusing on cross-border links, removal of bottlenecks, multimodal hubs and modern, safe and sustainable transport networks.

eligibility.company_type: EU Member States and, with their agreement, public or private undertakings and bodies (e.g. infrastructure managers, transport operators, ports, cities, regions)
requirements: Project located on, or directly serving, the TEN-T core or comprehensive network
Contribution to cross-border sections, bottleneck removal, missing links or key EU priorities (e.g. multimodal hubs, AFIF, military mobility) in line with the specific call text

funding_details.percentage: Typically up to 30% of eligible costs for works (up to 50% for studies/priority actions and up to 85% for cohesion-funded projects)
funding_details.typical_project: Large infrastructure projects with EU contribution often in the range of EUR 10–100+ million, depending on mode and call

focus_areas: Multimodal transport and traffic management systems
Alternative fuels infrastructure and military mobility (specific calls)
programs.deadline: Recurring calls under the CEF Transport work programme (usually yearly; exact deadlines defined in each call)

programs.name: Connecting Europe Facility (CEF) for Energy
programs.description: EU grants for trans-European energy infrastructure, supporting cross-border electricity, gas, hydrogen, smart grids, CO2 networks and cross-border renewable energy projects under the TEN-E policy.

eligibility.company_type: Energy companies, TSOs and other public or private legal entities (project developers, public authorities, NGOs, research institutions, etc.) established in eligible countries, usually with the agreement of the concerned Member States.
requirements: Project is on the official Union list of Projects of Common Interest (PCI) or Projects of Mutual Interest (PMI), or holds CB RES status for cross-border renewable energy.
Cross-border energy infrastructure with impact on at least two countries and contributing to TEN-E objectives (market integration, security of supply, decarbonisation).

funding_details.percentage: Up to 50% of eligible costs for studies and works (with higher co-funding rates, up to about 70–75%, possible for certain projects such as outermost regions or high security-of-supply/solidarity cases).
funding_details.typical_project: Large cross-border infrastructure projects, with EU contributions often in the range of EUR 10–100+ million for works on PCIs/PMIs.

focus_areas: Smart Grids and digitalised energy systems
programs.deadline: Typically one PCI/PMI call per year for energy infrastructure, plus separate windows for cross-border renewable energy; exact deadlines are defined in each call fiche.

programs.name: CEF Digital
programs.description: Funding for digital connectivity infrastructure.

eligibility.company_type: Companies and public-sector organisations (legal entities, public or private bodies)
requirements: Digital connectivity infrastructure project (e.g. 5G corridors, backbone networks, cross-border connectivity)
Pan-European relevance and alignment with CEF Digital work programme priorities
Applicants established in eligible countries as defined in each call (typically EU Member States and associated countries)

funding_details.percentage: Co-funding rates typically between 30% and 75% of eligible costs depending on action type, location and call conditions; some coordination and support actions may be funded up to 100%.
funding_details.typical_project: Single-project EU contributions usually range from a few million up to several tens of millions of euros (roughly EUR 5–50 million), depending on scope.

programs.deadline: Calls are launched periodically under the CEF Work Programmes; each call has its own deadline on the EU Funding & Tenders Portal.

programs.name: Nordic Green Growth Research and Innovation Programme
programs.provider: NordForsk / Nordic Innovation / Nordic Energy Research
programs.description: Joint Nordic research and innovation programme (2016–2020) that funded large projects on green growth to accelerate the transition towards a sustainable Nordic society, promoting green economic growth, sustainability and competitiveness.

eligibility.company_type: Nordic research organisations, companies, public-sector bodies, NGOs and other organisations based in the Nordic countries.
requirements: Consortium involving partner institutions/industry from at least three Nordic countries, with the host entity based in a Nordic country.
Project clearly contributes to green growth (e.g. low-carbon and resource-efficient solutions, circular economy, sustainable regional development and competitiveness) as defined in the call text.

funding_details.percentage: For industry-driven projects (Module II), public funding (including Nordic Innovation and other public sources) could cover up to around 50% of total project costs; co-funding was encouraged for research-driven projects (Module I).
funding_details.typical_project: Total programme budget was NOK 73 million for six projects; individual projects typically had total budgets around EUR 1–1.5 million, with Nordic funding covering up to about half for industry-driven projects.

programs.deadline: One-off call in 2016 (programme 2016–2020, now closed; no current recurring calls under this specific programme).

programs.name: Nordic Innovation – Digitalisation, AI & Data (various calls)
programs.description: Digitalisation and AI-related programmes and calls that fund Nordic cross-border innovation projects using data and artificial intelligence.

eligibility.company_type: Nordic companies and organisations (exact eligibility defined in each call).
requirements: Applicants based and operating in one or more Nordic countries.
Normally a Nordic consortium with partners from at least three Nordic countries (see specific call text).
Project aligned with the digitalisation, AI or data theme of the relevant call.

funding_details.percentage: Nordic Innovation usually requires at least 50% co-funding from project partners, and in many calls public funding (including Nordic Innovation) may not exceed 50% of total project costs; always check the specific call text.
funding_details.typical_project: Funding amounts vary by call; for example, the 'Applied Ethical AI on Nordic Patient Records' call provided NOK 5.8 million in grant funding for a single AI project with at least 50% co-financing.

programs.deadline: Individual calls with their own deadlines; there is no single recurring annual 'digital transformation' call.

programs.name: Co-Creation
programs.description: Funding for research organizations to develop a new research idea together with companies so that it can evolve into a joint Co-Innovation project. The aim is to create significant international business opportunities for companies and enable high-level scientific research in the research organization.

eligibility.company_type: Research and knowledge-dissemination organisations (e.g. universities, universities of applied sciences, research institutions)
requirements: Applicant is a research or knowledge-dissemination organisation whose main goal is to independently conduct basic or industrial research or experimental development, or widely disseminate results through teaching, publications or data transfer
Research organisation and companies want to develop a new research idea and its potential together OR build a new consortium and competence network and engage companies in joint development
Idea has high potential and broad applicability and can lead to a joint Co-Innovation project and new international business for Finnish companies
Project plan focuses on demonstrating the relevance and demand of the idea, engaging companies and building a business and international cooperation network
Application and brief project plan submitted via Business Finland’s funding e-service in line with Co-Creation call instructions

funding_details.percentage: Business Finland covers 80% of the accepted total project costs; the research organisation’s self-financing share is 20%.
funding_details.max_amount: Total project costs may not exceed EUR 100,000 per idea (even if several research organisations participate, the combined maximum remains EUR 100,000).
funding_details.cost_model: Funding is based on an overhead cost multiplier of 20% and an indirect personnel cost multiplier of 50% for eligible personnel costs; eligible costs include salaries and wages, indirect personnel costs, overheads, travel, materials and supplies, and necessary purchased services, while e.g. research work, grants, marketing and equipment investments are not accepted as project costs.

programs.deadline: Continuous application (Co-Creation funding can be applied for at all times; call information and any updates are provided on the service page).
